_read_me: The words every door's evidence file uses: the gateway, the website and the SDK each read a byte-identical copy of this file (agentx_sdk/, backend/, ui/utils/). Edit all three or none; a test fails when they differ. Words travel between doors; rules do not.

verdicts.RECOVERED: Blocked, agent told why, then a later call to the same tool ran
verdicts.HELD: Held for a person, not approved; did not run
verdicts.REFUSED: Not run: no verdict could be had
verdicts.HALTED: Halted as a runaway loop; did not run

notes.before_you_share: This file names your own agents, tools and the sites in their calls, as your code sent them. Check it before you send it to others outside your organization.

hosted.about: AgentX evidence for one hosted gateway key: the rules in force, the built-in checks that are off on this gateway and why, the calls that were stopped or held, the sites recorded for calls the gateway allowed (a site can be missing, none is added), and who can change the rules. The calls' own text is not included. A list that is null could not be read when this file was produced (could_not_read names it); an empty list was read and holds nothing. In allowlists, a null tools or sites means that agent is not limited.
hosted.who_can_change: The built-in rules: AgentX, by deploying the gateway (a new version or a changed setting). Which tools and sites each agent may use (the allowlist above): anyone holding this key, with agentx allowlist push. On the hosted gateway the agent's own process holds that key too, so an agent able to run that command could change its own list. Nothing here records who pushed a list, only when it was last pushed.
hosted.rules_fingerprint: Changes when a rule in force, one of its listed limits, or the gateway version changes; some settings, such as the dependency check's thresholds, do not move it. Compare it between two downloads to see whether the rules changed.
hosted.stopped_or_held_calls: For each stopped or held call: "verdict" is what the gateway did when it stopped or held it, "status" is where it stands now (the two can differ, for example once a held call was answered with this gateway key, which the agent may also hold, or once the agent changed course after a block), and "outcome" says both in words. "receipt_id" is the gateway's id for that record, so one call can be named exactly. "sites" lists hosts a call was addressed to, at most 8, in name order (the host only, never the rest of the address; one part of a name that is 20 or more characters and mixes letters and digits, the shape of most tokens, is shown as [withheld]. A secret split across shorter parts, or made only of digits or only of letters, is still shown, and some ordinary names, such as an S3 bucket or a preview deployment, are withheld too). They are read from the call as the gateway kept it, the way the site list reads an allowed call, such as an http:// address in a url argument, an internal one the call was stopped for included. [] means no site was read from it, which can happen for a call that did name one: an address with no http:// in a command, one in an argument such as webhook on some tools, a call the SDK's own word list stopped, or an address past the first 16 KB of an argument. A listed site can be the one a call was allowed to reach while the site it was stopped for sat in another argument, such as a webhook beside a url. null means the record keeps nothing to read it from. A call that only would have been stopped while the SDK watched is not in this list: it ran, and it is listed under ran_while_watching. A hold or a halted run from an SDK older than 0.4.28 is listed even while it watched.
hosted.ran_while_watching: The stops and holds this gateway returned while the SDK watched, where the SDK runs the call anyway, from gateway 2026.10.20.2 on; each of those calls ran. Newest first, at most the same number as the stopped list, and deleted with the allowed calls, oldest first. "rule" is the rule that would have stopped or held it, or "Agent's request for a person" when the agent asked for one. "verdict" is what the gateway would have done: CHALLENGED or DENIED, stopped; ESCALATED, held for a person. "watch_source" is what set watch, as the SDK said: AGENTX_POSTURE, or "tool option" for a tool's own posture setting; null when the SDK did not say (an older SDK). "sites" is read and shown the way the stopped list's is. ran_while_watching_by_rule counts every such call kept, per rule, including any the list does not show: one run reading a table one row at a time while watching is recorded on every read and can fill the list. Not here: a hold or a halted run from an SDK older than 0.4.28, which is in the stopped list; the loop and repeat stops, which this gateway gives a watching SDK only before 0.4.28 (those are in the stopped list); any call on a gateway that sends its records to a control plane; and a call the SDK's own check decided itself, which is only on the developer's machine (agentx evidence): every call watched before 2026.10.20.2, and since then one an older SDK matched, one matched with AGENTX_SHIELD_ASKS_GATEWAY set off, and one the developer's own files also stop (their site allowlist file, or a word their policies file added). Not covered by record_head.
hosted.sites_recorded: For each agent, each site with the number of allowed calls that named it, back to "sites_since" in records_kept. A call that ran while the SDK watched although this gateway would have stopped it is not counted here; its sites are listed with it under ran_while_watching.
hosted.record_head: The record's latest entry when this file was made. To check later that the record was not rewritten since, open the Evidence page with ?head=<this value> added to its address; it says whether that entry still matches. It covers the stopped or held calls, not the sites or the calls that ran while watching.
hosted.rule_sources: Each place this gateway's rules come from, and whether it was read when this file was made. "policy_store" is the gateway's own rule store; "rules_file" is the file of rules a developer added on this gateway. "read"; "no file" (nothing there, so nothing from it); "damaged" (it exists and could not be understood); "could not open" (the system refused to open it). A state followed by ", earlier copy in force" means the gateway could not read the file now and still uses the rules it last read from it, and those switched on are listed in rules_in_force; without an earlier copy, no rule from it is in force.
hosted.record_not_intact: The record was changed outside AgentX since it was written, so it is not intact.
hosted.sql_checks: The SQL checks catch the common destructive and bulk-read shapes, not every spelling. Known ways past them: a WHERE hidden behind a comment (-- or #), a statement written with no spaces, two statements on one line, a LIMIT with a fraction, a MERGE whose ON compares a column with itself, COPY ... TO or INTO OUTFILE, SUM or AVG over one-row groups, and a statement the parser cannot read. To limit what an agent can reach whatever the spelling, give it only the tools it needs (a tool allowlist).
hosted.answered_with_key: The gateway sees a key, not a person, and only its own log names which key answered a held call. On the hosted gateway that is this key, which the agent's own process also holds, so "then approved" means the key approved it, not necessarily a person.

local.about: AgentX evidence from one developer's machine: the rules this machine's AgentX checks agent calls against, the rules switched off and what still runs, the calls it stopped or would have stopped while watching (each with the site it was addressed to, where one was recorded), the calls held for a person and not approved, the calls it did not run because no verdict could be had, the calls it halted as a runaway loop, the sites recorded for calls it allowed (a site can be missing, none is added), the outbound allowlist itself, and the record's latest entry. The calls' own text is not included. A list that is null could not be read when this file was produced; an empty list was read and holds nothing. Fields this machine has no source for are named in "not_on_this_door", never filled in.
local.rules_in_force: Each description says what the rule stops when blocking is on. While watching, a call it would stop runs, and is listed below as "Would have been stopped; ran (watching)".
local.outbound_allowlist: For each agent the allowlist limits, the only sites its calls may reach. {} means no agent is limited, so calls may reach any site. An agent listed with [] may reach no site. null means the allowlist file could not be read, and every call to a site is stopped when blocking is on.
local.rule_sources: Each place this machine's rules come from, and whether it was read when this file was made: "read"; "no file" (nothing there, so nothing from it); "damaged" (it exists and could not be understood); "could not open" (the system refused to open it); "earlier import file" (the rules file holds an import file from an earlier version, so no rules were added); "could not read" (it could not be looked at, so whether it holds rules is not known). A rule from a source that was not read is not in rules_in_force, except an allowlist that could not be read, which is listed there because it stops every call to a site. A policies file that could not be read stops every protected call when blocking is on (unless AGENTX_POLICY_LOAD=permissive); while watching, calls run on the built-in rules only.
local.who_can_change: Anyone who can write this project's .agentx folder or its policies file. The fingerprint changes when the rules do; nothing here records who changed them.
local.rules_fingerprint: Changes when any rule in force, an adopted rule, the outbound allowlist or the SDK version changes. Compare it between two files from this machine to see whether the rules changed. It is not comparable with a hosted gateway's fingerprint.
local.stopped_or_held_calls: For each call: "verdict" says in words what this machine did, and "status" is the value it recorded. A call stopped while watching ran, and is listed as "Would have been stopped; ran (watching)". A call listed as "Not run: no verdict could be had" was not run because no check could answer for it, for example the gateway could not be reached with blocking set to fail closed, or the API key was refused; "rule" names the reason. "ledger_id" is the record's id for that call, so one call can be named exactly. "sites" lists the hosts the record kept for each call, at most 8, in name order (the host only, never the rest of the address; one part of a name that is 20 or more characters and mixes letters and digits, the shape of most tokens, is shown as [withheld]. A secret split across shorter parts, or made only of digits or only of letters, is still shown, and some ordinary names, such as an S3 bucket or a preview deployment, are withheld too). They are read from a web address in the arguments named as an address or a command, such as url or command, wherever it sits in that text, a comment included. [] means none was kept for that call: it named none that way, on some tools the address sat in another argument, such as notify(webhook=...) (the outbound allowlist still checks it), the row was written before this machine kept sites, or it is an agentx-mcp row for a call stopped before it was sent, such as a held tool change. A listed site can be the one a call was allowed to reach while the site it was stopped for sat in another argument, such as a webhook beside a url. null means this machine's record is older than its sites.
local.server_changes: What an MCP server changed in the tools it offers, as agentx-mcp's tool pinning saw it: "what" is the change, and "held_then" says whether pinning held the tool for approval at the time (null for a record an older version wrote, which did not say). These are not calls: no list or count of calls in this file includes them.
local.sites_recorded: For each agent, each site with the number of allowed calls that named it.
local.record_head: The record's latest entry when this file was made. To check later that the record was not rewritten since, run in the same project: agentx audit --record --head <this value>
local.records_kept: Records older than "days" are deleted. This machine has one limit for all its records together, not one per list, so "max_stopped_or_held_calls" and "max_allowed_calls" are the same number ("max_rows_shared"): past it, most allowed calls are deleted first, oldest first, and if that is not enough, the oldest records of any kind. The stopped or held list goes back to "stopped_or_held_since" and the sites to "sites_since"; a list named in "period_unknown" holds a call with no recorded date, so its period cannot be stated.
local.sql_checks: The SQL checks catch the common destructive and bulk-read shapes, not every spelling. Known ways past them: a WHERE hidden behind a comment (-- or #), a statement written with no spaces, two statements on one line, a LIMIT with a fraction, MERGE, COPY ... TO or INTO OUTFILE, SUM or AVG over one-row groups, and a statement the parser cannot read. To limit what an agent can reach whatever the spelling, give it only the tools it needs (a tool allowlist, which a gateway enforces when your agent runs with an API key; this machine's checks do not).

record_checks.matches: Entry {n} still matches: the record was not rewritten since.
record_checks.rewritten: Entry {n} no longer matches: this record was rewritten.
record_checks.too_old: Entry {n} is older than this record keeps, so it cannot be checked.
record_checks.missing: Entry {n} is missing: this record was rewritten or cut short.
record_checks.no_record: There is no record here to check entry {n} against.
record_checks.not_a_head: That is not a record entry from an evidence file.
record_checks.local_head: Entry {n} is from a local evidence file, made on a developer's machine. Check it there with: agentx audit --record --head <the value>

local.receipt_id: Empty: this file holds only a gateway's receipts. Each call's "ledger_id" is given instead; from version 0.5.6, a Python agent stopped by this machine's check, with no gateway receipt, was given "local-" and that ledger_id as its receipt_id.
local.applies_to: This machine's rules read a call's text, not a list of which kinds of call they apply to, so there is nothing true to put here.

hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111115: Blocks some file paths: one that climbs two or more folders up (../../etc/passwd; a single ../, or one written as %2e%2e/, is not caught), and reads of some credential and secret files, such as an SSH key, ~/.aws/credentials, a gcloud credentials file, ~/.netrc, ~/.pgpass, a .env file, /etc/shadow and the Windows SAM file (C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM). Not caught, among others: ~/.kube/config, saving the SAM with reg save, and a path outside the working folder written in full, such as /home/other/notes.txt.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111102: On some database reads that can return customer personal data, such as a SELECT naming an email or phone column, the call runs and the AgentX Python SDK removes the values it recognises, such as email addresses and US-style phone numbers, from the result before the agent sees it. Not every result shape or spelling is covered, and while the SDK is watching rather than blocking nothing is removed.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111119: Blocks a call whose text carries a hidden direction-override character (U+202D, U+202E) or an invisible tag character (U+E0000 to U+E007F). Neither has a legitimate use in a tool call. Characters that do appear in ordinary text, such as zero-width spaces, are not blocked by this check.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111120: Blocks some forms of mass network scanning with nmap, masscan or zmap, such as scanning all ports (-p-), version scanning, or a network range wider than /24. Not every scanner, flag or range spelling is caught. Some scans whose only targets are the machine itself, such as nmap -sV localhost, are not blocked. A simple check of one host is allowed.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111122: Blocks a command that opens a reverse shell or a raw remote-control connection: a bash /dev/tcp or /dev/udp device, netcat with -e or -c, socat running a shell, a mkfifo and netcat pipe, or some in-code forms that wire a socket to a shell, such as a Python one-liner using os.dup2; the same in other languages (Perl, Ruby, PHP, PowerShell) is not caught. A plain port check (nc -z) and an ordinary socket client are allowed. It reads the command a tool call carries, not connections the agent's own process opens.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111101: Blocks statements that destroy table data with no limit: DROP TABLE, DROP SCHEMA, DROP DATABASE, TRUNCATE, and a DELETE or UPDATE with nothing limiting it to specific rows. A drop of a table or database named by a CREATE the gateway allowed earlier in the same run can be held for a person instead, but only on a gateway where approving a held call needs a separate admin key; with a key from the website, or on a gateway with one key, it is blocked, because that key can also approve held calls. The gateway cannot see whether that CREATE succeeded, so the object may have existed before. A change limited by a real WHERE clause is not blocked by this check, though it can still be sent to a model check. The same rule also blocks some spellings of an HTTP DELETE on _all or a wildcard, such as curl -X DELETE; other clients, such as requests.delete or Invoke-RestMethod, are not caught. It also blocks cloud teardown such as terraform destroy, a recursive delete of a root, home or system folder, formatting or raw writes to a disk, and a fork bomb.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111103: Blocks a call carrying a web address, written with http:// or https://, as a whole argument, or, in some spellings, as the address a curl, wget or PowerShell iwr or irm command fetches (such as curl localhost:3000), that points inside the network: localhost and other loopback addresses (127.x, ::1, 0.0.0.0), cloud metadata services (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal), link-local addresses, and private ranges (10.x, 172.16 to 172.31.x, 192.168.x, IPv6 fd00::/8), including some encoded and short spellings such as http://2130706433/ and http://127.1/, and names ending in .internal. Not caught, among others: an address with no http:// given to another program (nc localhost 6379), and a short form with no http:// (curl 127.1). A web address whose name resolves to a loopback, link-local or metadata address is blocked too; one that resolves to a private range is not, and neither is the shared range 100.64.0.0/10. Public addresses are allowed. On web requests, a mention of localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 or 169.254.169.254 anywhere in the call also sends it to a model check.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111104: Blocks a call that reads credentials or bulk personal data, or sends them out. Reads: naming a credential to read (SELECT password, read_config('db_password'), os.environ['STRIPE_API_KEY']), SELECT * on a sensitive table such as users, customers or secrets (a WHERE clause does not exempt it; LIMIT 1 does on some tables), or reading credential or personal-data columns (password, api_key, email, phone, ssn) with no WHERE clause. Sends: any request to a paste or capture site (pastebin.com, webhook.site, a Discord, Slack or Telegram webhook), or a request to an outside host carrying a private key, a GitHub, Stripe, AWS or Slack token not bound for its own provider, two or more Social Security numbers, or an upload that names a sensitive table in some spellings, such as table=users. A lookup of one record that names its columns (SELECT email FROM users WHERE id = 42), a password mentioned in ordinary text, and a secret written to a log or chat with no outside web address are not blocked by this check; on database queries, reads naming email, role or system_users can also be sent to a model check.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111107: Blocks a command that downloads a script and runs it in the same step: curl, wget or PowerShell's Invoke-WebRequest piped into a shell or interpreter such as bash, sh, python or node, PowerShell's iwr or irm piped into iex, and iex written before a DownloadString or an irm (iex (irm https://...)). A script block built from the download ([scriptblock]::Create) is not caught. Downloading a file without running it is allowed, and so is a plain pip or npm install (those are checked by Unverified Dependency Approval). Later in the same run, running a refused script after downloading it separately is blocked too.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111105: On database queries, sends a statement that drops a schema or changes database-level settings (the words drop schema or alter database, or a statement close in meaning) to a model check, which can stop it. DROP SCHEMA and DROP DATABASE are blocked under Mass Destructive Intent (a DROP DATABASE named by a CREATE allowed earlier in the same run can be held for a person instead, on a gateway where approving a held call needs a separate admin key). Reading the catalog (information_schema, pg_catalog, sqlite_master, PRAGMA table_info) is not checked. If the model check cannot be reached, or the account's daily model checks are used up, the call runs.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111113: Holds a call until it is approved when its text pairs a publishing word (publish, post, share, send, announce, broadcast, tweet) with a destination named in words, such as Twitter or X, LinkedIn, Reddit, Medium, a forum, threads, a blog, a newsletter, a press release, a website or publicly. Some wording is held on its own, such as publish the article or go live with. It reads wording, not the service being called or whether the destination is really public: create_post(platform='linkedin') with no such words is not held, while post the results to the internal forum is, and so can an ordinary message that mentions something public.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111116: Holds a call until it is approved when it would delete a whole mailbox or every message: wording such as delete all emails, empty the inbox or purge the mailbox, a Gmail batchDelete, an IMAP flag-all-deleted or doveadm expunge, or a declared delete action given an all scope or an empty search. It reads wording, so a request like delete all threads older than a year is held too. Deleting one message by id is not held, though some calls that also name the inbox or mailbox are. Empty the trash or empty the spam folder is not held, but delete all messages in trash is.
hosted.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111117: Before an install written as a command, such as pip, uv pip, poetry, npm, yarn or pnpm install, runs, looks each named package up on PyPI or npm and holds the call until it is approved if the package is not there, was first published less than 14 days ago, or has a name close to a popular package (such as reqeusts for requests) without signs it is genuine: a provenance record, the same publisher, or over 100,000 weekly downloads. A private package that is not on the public registry is held too. If the registry does not answer within about 1.5 seconds, the install is allowed. These limits are the defaults, which a deployment's settings can change. Installs from a requirements file, a git address or a local path, and other package managers such as cargo, go, gem or brew, are not checked.
hosted.a339b81f-0607-42d8-b0c2-9c2b221dd646: Checks text that a client sends to the gateway's prompt-check address for instructions that try to override an agent's task: first a fixed phrase list (such as ignore all previous, you are now, forget your instructions, jailbreak), then a model check. A match is recorded and answered as challenged; the caller decides whether to drop the text. The AgentX SDK and MCP proxy do not send anything to this check, so fetched web pages and tool output are not scanned unless your own code sends them. If the model check fails or the account's daily model checks are used up, only the phrase list applies.

local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111101: Stops SQL that destroys table data with nothing limiting it, for example DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE TABLE, and a DELETE or UPDATE with no WHERE clause. A change limited by a real WHERE clause is allowed. Only some spellings are recognised.
local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111103: Stops a call that names a loopback or cloud-metadata address, for example localhost, 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, a common path to a cloud's internal credentials. On Claude Code the developer's own machine (localhost, any 127.x address, ::1 or 0.0.0.0, in any spelling) is allowed; a cloud-metadata or private address is still stopped. Only some spellings are recognised.
local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111104: Stops a call that reads credentials or sends data to a paste site, for example SELECT password or SELECT api_key, or a pastebin.com or webhook.site address. Only some spellings are recognised.
local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111102: Stops a database read that returns customer personal data in bulk, for example SELECT email, phone FROM customers. When the SQL is passed as its own argument, reading one person's record with WHERE id = ..., or with LIMIT 1, is allowed; the same read inside a shell command (psql -c '...') is stopped. Only some spellings are recognised.
local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111115: Stops a file path that climbs two or more folders up (../../), or that reads a credentials file, for example an SSH key, AWS credentials, a .env file or /etc/shadow. Only some spellings are recognised.
local.22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222106: Stops commands that destroy a machine: a recursive delete (rm -r -f, rd /s, Remove-Item -Recurse) of the root, a home folder, a drive or some system folders; writing onto a raw disk with dd, cat, cp or tee; formatting, wiping or repartitioning a disk or drive (mkfs, wipefs -a, shred, sgdisk, blkdiscard, parted mklabel, Format-Volume, format C:); a fork bomb; and some spellings of a script piped into a shell, such as curl ... | bash or PowerShell's iwr ... | iex (iex written before the download, iex (irm ...), is not caught). Deleting a folder inside the project (rm -rf ./build, also when the call names the project as the folder it runs in), reading a disk (dd if=/dev/sda of=disk.img) and formatting an image file (mkfs.ext4 disk.img) are allowed. A delete under some system folders (/var, /usr, C:\Windows) is stopped even when it is a project there (/var/www/app) or cleanup (C:\Windows\Temp), while a named folder in a system temp area (/var/tmp/build) is allowed. Other system folders, such as /opt or C:\ProgramData, are not checked. Cloud teardown such as terraform destroy is not checked here.
local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111119: Stops a call whose text carries a hidden direction-override character (U+202D, U+202E) or an invisible tag character (U+E0000 to U+E007F). Zero-width spaces are not stopped.
local.11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111122: Stops a command that opens a reverse shell or a raw remote-control connection, for example a bash /dev/tcp device, netcat with -e, or socat running a shell. A plain port check (nc -z) is allowed.

watched_verdicts.ESCALATED: Would have been held for a person; ran (watching)
